claims.text: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools.
claims.excerpt: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools.

claims.text: A CLAUDE.md file gives Claude persistent instructions for a project, and Claude reads it at the start of every session.
claims.excerpt: CLAUDE.md files are markdown files that give Claude persistent instructions for a project, your personal workflow, or your entire organization. You write these files in plain text; Claude reads them at the start of every session.

claims.text: In plan mode, Claude reads files and proposes a plan, and it makes no edits until you approve.
claims.excerpt: Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve.

claims.text: To make a skill, create a SKILL.md file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit.
claims.excerpt: Create a SKILL.md file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit.

claims.text: Hooks are user-defined shell commands that Claude Code runs at set points in its lifecycle, so certain actions always happen.
claims.excerpt: Hooks are user-defined shell commands. Claude Code runs them at specific points in its lifecycle, which gives you deterministic control: certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them.

claims.text: A subagent is a specialized AI assistant for one type of task, useful when a side task would flood your main conversation.
claims.excerpt: Subagents are specialized AI assistants that handle specific types of tasks. Use one when a side task would flood your main conversation with search results, logs, or file contents

claims.text: When Claude says it is done and it is not, the usual cause is that it had no way to check its own work.
claims.excerpt: Claude said it was done and it wasn’t quite, usually because it had no way to check its own work.

claims.text: Running /clear between tasks is still worth doing, because a focused context gets better answers and costs less.
claims.excerpt: /clear between tasks is still worth doing, because a focused context gets you better answers and costs less.

claims.text: Claude Code supports fine-grained permissions, so you can set what the agent may do and what it may not.
claims.excerpt: Claude Code supports fine-grained permissions so that you can specify exactly what the agent is allowed to do and what it can’t.
